originalPrompt: 4WD obstacle-avoiding robot car with ultrasonic sensors front and back and LED lights
projectDescription: 4wd Obstacle-avoiding Robot built around a Raspberry Pi Pico W with HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance (4 m), WS2812B RGB LED Strip (30 LEDs, 1 m), N20 Micro Gear Motor 6 V 300 rpm, DRV8833 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver; battery-powered (≈4.8 h per charge), housed in a PETG enclosure.
plan:
- Main Controller: Raspberry Pi Pico W — $6.00/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Distance Sensor 1: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance (4 m) — $1.20/unit; named in the prompt: ultrasonic
- Distance Sensor 2: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance (4 m) — $1.20/unit; named in the prompt: ultrasonic
- LED Strip: WS2812B RGB LED Strip (30 LEDs, 1 m) — $2.80/unit; named in the prompt: led
- Drive Motor 1: N20 Micro Gear Motor 6 V 300 rpm — $2.80/unit
- Drive Motor 2: N20 Micro Gear Motor 6 V 300 rpm — $2.80/unit
- Drive Motor 3: N20 Micro Gear Motor 6 V 300 rpm — $2.80/unit
- Drive Motor 4: N20 Micro Gear Motor 6 V 300 rpm — $2.80/unit
- Motor Driver 1: DRV8833 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver — $0.90/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Motor Driver 2: DRV8833 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver — $0.90/unit; lowest price among candidates
- Level Shifter 1: 4-ch Bidirectional Level Shifter (BSS138) — protects 3.3 V GPIO from 5 V signals / meets 5 V input thresholds
- Level Shifter 2: 4-ch Bidirectional Level Shifter (BSS138) — protects 3.3 V GPIO from 5 V signals / meets 5 V input thresholds
- Battery: 18650 Li-ion 3000 mAh + Holder — $4.00/unit; matches rechargeable
- USB-C Charger + Protection: TP4056 USB-C Li-ion Charger + Protection — 1S Li-ion needs CC/CV charging and over-discharge protection
- 5V Boost: TPS61088 Boost Converter Module (5 V 3 A) — $3.50/unit; boost: 2.8–4.2 V → 5 V, 3000 mA ≥ peak 2130 mA
- Power: li-ion 10.8 Wh, est. runtime 4.8 h
- Enclosure: 110×125×35 mm in PETG

subSteps.title: Cut / machine the structural plate and deburr edges
Test-fit boards on standoffs before wiring
Assemble the power path (battery, charger, regulators)
Distribute the VBAT rail to 4 load(s)
Connect Motor Driver 1 outputs to 2 load(s)
Connect Motor Driver 2 outputs to 2 load(s)
Insert level shifters (LV = 3.3 V side, HV = 5 V side)
Verify continuity and rail voltages before inserting the MCU
Run actuators at low duty first (soft-start) and check driver temperature
Mount boards and modules inside the enclosure
Mount external actuators/sensors and route cables
Fasten the enclosure onto the chassis plate
Close the enclosure and fasten the lid

issues.message: Distance Sensor 1 uses 5 V logic but Raspberry Pi Pico W is 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant.
issues.fix: A BSS138 level shifter is inserted in these signal lines by the wiring stage.

issues.message: Distance Sensor 2 uses 5 V logic but Raspberry Pi Pico W is 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant.
issues.fix: A BSS138 level shifter is inserted in these signal lines by the wiring stage.

issues.message: LED Strip uses 5 V logic but Raspberry Pi Pico W is 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant.
issues.fix: A BSS138 level shifter is inserted in these signal lines by the wiring stage.

issues.message: 18650 Li-ion 3000 mAh + Holder gives ≈3.9 h, below the 4 h target.
issues.fix: Use a larger pack or parallel cells.

issues.message: VBAT rail peak 4177 mA exceeds 3000 mA source rating.
issues.fix: Choose a higher-current regulator or split the rail.
